// P4 porch in the angle: bench, wash stand, hanging lantern. Inner air x49..52, y3..5, z9..11 (the box in rooms.json).
// Lane kept clear: x51 from the steps (51,3,8) to the wing door (51,3,12), and (52,3,10) in front of the gable's door (53,3,10).
// Posts at (49,9), (52,9), (49,11) belong to the porch run (fittings), so the furniture stands on column x50 and the corner.
import { chair } from "../vocab.mjs";
import { layers } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs";

export function build(g) {
  // Two seats: a bench-side chair on the north row and a chair on the west side, both facing the table at (50,3..4,10).

  chair(g, 49, 3, 10, "east");

  // Table (fence leg + top slab), barrel wash stand with a flower pot, basin cauldron in the corner, lantern on the table.
  layers(g, [49, 3, 9], {
    T: ["spruce_fence", {}],
    B: ["barrel", { facing: "up", open: "false" }],
    W: ["water_cauldron", { level: "3" }],

      " B W",
    ],
    [
      "    ",
      " P  ",
      " F  ",
    ],
    [
      "    ",
      " L  ",
      "    ",
    ],
  ]);
}

input.summary:
P4 porch in the angle (parts/room-27.mjs) now builds clean: the barrel wash stand is dropped because its only free cell (50,3,11) is the wing window's sill from an earlier part.
Table, basin cauldron, flower pot and lantern stay as before. make.sh exits 0 and writes build.nbt; the porch line reports placed 6, refused 0, offPalette [].
No palette swaps were needed (offPalette was already empty).
left: Only one seat is in the porch: chair(g, 50, 3, 9, "south") is silently skipped because the porch rail birch_fence at (50,3,9) (fittings, earlier part) occupies that cell. chair() returns a count and the part ignores it, so runParts never reports it. Not in this fix scope; a free cell is needed or the bench chair must be dropped deliberately.
The barrel wash stand is gone. Nothing else in the porch's y3 layer can take it: x51 is the lane and the other cells are taken.

Outside this part, make.sh still reports REFUSED for P3 upper landing, P4 wing kitchen, P4 attic bedroom, P5 barn aisle and stalls, and P5 hay loft. Those are other parts' problems and were left alone.
A birch_fence at (51,3,11) sits on the x51 lane (the walk from the steps to the wing door) in an earlier part's output; flag it to the fittings/shell owner.

waste.what: Worked out which porch cells were free at y3 by reading each cell one at a time with a node one-liner, to find a spot for the refused barrel and to see that the chair had been silently skipped.
waste.cost: about 36 single-cell lookups plus 2 retries of the lookup script; the lane and occupancy reasoning was done by hand
waste.tool: `mcd plan build.nbt --rooms rooms.json --only "P4 porch in the angle"` shows occupancy but only at y4 by default; it needs a --y 3 option, a lane/keep-clear overlay (from the plan's Notes), and a free-cell listing for the room's box. Also the helpers (chair, window sill, shutter) should return refusals to runParts so a silently skipped chair shows in parts-report.json, not only in a count nobody reads.

waste.what: Chose drop-vs-move for the refused barrel by hand: checked each candidate against the lane rule and the part's comment, then edited the layers() rows and the comment.
waste.cost: one Edit plus one make.sh rerun (about 40 s)
waste.tool: runParts could offer a refusal-suggest mode that lists free cells inside the room box that are not keep-clear, so a refused block can be moved without hand-checking the lane each time.
